newsitem.title: NORWAY: Bank shares drive up Norwegian stock index.
newsitem.headline: Bank shares drive up Norwegian stock index.

text.p: Brisk trade in bank shares helped push the Norwegian Total index to an all-time high of 866.65 points in early trade on Monday.
But business later levelled off and the index closed at 864.30, up only 0.13 percent from Friday. Turnover was a moderate 696 million crowns.

"I think think we will calm down a bit this week but market sentiment is positive," one dealer said. "The markets in Europe are still strong, there is good turnover in finance shares and interest rates continue to be low."
Den norske Bank (DnB), Norway's largest commercial bank, rose 1.44 percent to 21.20 crowns and accounted for 81.4 million crowns of trade.
Oil company Saga Petroleum, which last week reported healthy eight-month profits, also did well, its A share climbing 3.64 percent to 114 crowns.
On Friday the Total index set a new all-time high for the third consecutive session after weaker than expected U.S. nonfarm payroll figures sent stock markets climbing.
